name: Garawa
catalog_quote: In Garawa primary stress (indicated in this section by ') is always on the first syllable of the phonological word. Primary stress is manifested by loudness, high pitch and length. ... Secondary stress ... occurs on the penultimate syllable of words with four or more syllables. audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-strict; initial primary, penult secondary in 4+ syllable words, alternating tertiary leftward skipping syllable 2) is exactly Furby 1974 section 5, p.10, verified verbatim in the held PDF, and is independently echoed by two other held primary sources (Furby & Furby 1977:79; Belfrage 1992:67-68 with transcribed examples). The record itself, however, carries the evidence only in the database-audit fields (dq/dloc) with blank quote/cite/loc/grade: promote the Furby 1974:10 section 5 quotation into quote/cite/loc and grade it as a primary phonology source. The single unheld work that could refine the record is Mushin 2012 ch. 2 (paywalled; UQ repository copy restricted); nothing seen suggests it contradicts Furby, so no recode is indicated.

sources.note: Only modern reference grammar of Garrwa; its phonology chapter is the sole post-1974 first-hand statement on word stress (and on the stress domain over host=clitic, which Belfrage 1992 raises); our coding rests on a 12-page 1974 SIL phonology paper alone.
